links.outcome: LLM-judged empathy, safety and contextual understanding of RAG mental health chatbot responses
links.effect: Generalist models scored higher on empathy than domain-specific fine-tunes (3.72 vs. 3.26, p < 0.001); all models performed well on safety; generalists showed better contextual understanding.
links.quote: We find a clear trend: the generalist models outperform the domain-specific ones in empathy (3.72 vs. 3.26, $p < 0.001$) in spite of being much smaller (3B vs. 7B), and all models perform well in terms of safety, but the generalist models show better contextual understanding and are less prone to overfitting as we observe in the domain-specific models.

unlisted_practices: Choosing a general-purpose reasoning model over a mental-health-specific fine-tune for RAG-based counseling chatbots
Using LLM-as-a-judge for automated evaluation of empathy and safety in mental health dialogue

screen.reason: Evaluates generalist vs specialized fine-tuned LLM architectures within a standard RAG pipeline for mental health dialogue using benchmark evaluation; does not test a deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
